source: synthetic weather fixture, not live data
note: SYNTHETIC COMPETITION DEMO FIXTURE -- not Open-Meteo historical data and not a real forecast. Hand-authored TrailGuard replay asset for Phase 5 benchmark scenario B08 (a gust band that clears). The gusts are NON-MONOTONE on purpose: 21 km/h at 11:00, a 49 km/h band at 12:00, then back down to 22 km/h at 13:00 and 20 km/h at 14:00. With the scenario's analysis clock at 11:40 the hiker's projected arrivals read the 49 km/h row at NOW and at +30 and read the calm rows at +60 and +120, so the R-C gust threshold (45 km/h in the frozen rule pack) is crossed at exactly two horizons and cleared at the other two. A run that carries the gust band forward to +60 or +120 contradicts the core; a run that ignores it at NOW or +30 contradicts it there. Values are invented. precipitation_probability arrives in percent ('%' in hourly_units, exactly as open-meteo reports it) and must be divided by 100 to obtain the 0..1 probability the TrailGuard schemas use.
